topics.name: Kinds of sentences and end marks

options: We will learns new things this year.
We will learn new things this year.
We will learned new things this year.
questions.rule: After will, always use the base form of the verb: will learn.

options: Riya are in Grade Six now.
Riya am in Grade Six now.
Riya is in Grade Six now.
questions.rule: One person (he/she/Riya) takes is. am goes only with I; are with we/you/they.
In a question, the verb comes before the subject: Where is our classroom? (classroom is singular)

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: will is followed by the base form: will ring, not will rings.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: These books is plural, so the verb is are.

questions.after: wear our school uniform on Monday.
questions.rule: Modals like must never change: no -s, no -ing.

questions.after: join the art club this year.
questions.rule: For a plan, use am/is/are going to + base verb: going to join.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence about the new school year.
questions.rule: Subject + will + base verb + object: We will learn ...

chat: Will you join the drawing class this year?
questions.rule: Answer a will question with will + base verb: I will join.

chat: Is your brother in Grade Six too?
options: No, he are in Grade Four.
No, he is in Grade Four.
No, he am in Grade Four.
questions.rule: he is one person, so use is.

options: You should to revise your lessons every day.
You should revise your lessons every day.
You should revising your lessons every day.
questions.rule: After should, use the base verb without 'to': should revise.

options: Sameer is going play in the school band.
Sameer going to play in the school band.
Sameer is going to play in the school band.
questions.rule: The full pattern is is going to + base verb. Do not drop 'is' or 'to'.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: must is followed by the base verb: must come.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Each term is singular, so the present verb takes -s: brings.
The subject is students (plural), so use are.
Use How + adjective in exclamations: How exciting ...! (What needs a noun: What a day!)
Negative modal: should not + base verb.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence about a plan.
questions.rule: Plan: subject + is going to + base verb.

chat: Can you help me set the table?
options: Yes, I can to help you.
questions.rule: can + base verb, with no 'to' and no -s: can help.

chat: What are you going to do this weekend?
options: I am going to visit my grandparents.
I going to visit my grandparents.
I am going to visited my grandparents.
questions.rule: I am going to + base verb: I am going to visit.

options: The box of new crayons is on my desk.
The box of new crayons are on my desk.
The box of new crayons be on my desk.
questions.rule: The real subject is the box (one box), not crayons, so use is.
To ask permission: May I + base verb: May I come in?
A command (imperative) starts with the base verb: close.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: My sister and I = two people (we), so use are going to.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: should goes with both verbs: should be kind and (should) help them.
The future of is/am/are is will be.
Everyone is singular, so use has.
Wh-question: What + will + subject + base verb ... ?

chat: Does your father work in Pune?
questions.rule: In the simple present, he/she takes verb + -s: he works.

chat: Shall we start our project now?
questions.rule: Let's (let us) is followed by the base verb: let's start.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tenses.
options: Last year we wrote letters, and this year we will write stories.
Last year we write letters, and this year we will write stories.
Last year we wrote letters, and this year we will wrote stories.
questions.rule: Last year needs the past (wrote); will needs the base verb (write).

options: You must wear an helmet when you ride a bicycle.
You must wear a helmet when you ride a bicycle.
You must wears a helmet when you ride a bicycle.
questions.rule: helmet starts with a consonant sound, so a helmet; and must + base verb.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: old begins with a vowel sound, so use an: an old fort.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Yesterday needs the past, and students is plural: were.
Use on with days: on Monday.

questions.after: many new books in our library.
questions.rule: many new books is plural, so use There are.
will give + person (us) + thing (a new timetable).
Polite request: Could you + base verb ... ?

chat: Did you finish your homework? We will play cricket at five.
options: Yes, I finished it. I will come at five.
Yes, I finished it. I will coming at five.
Yes, I finishing it. I will come at five.
questions.rule: Finished work takes the past (finished); the plan takes will come.
They always takes are.

options: One of my friends is joining the school choir this year.
One of my friends are joining the school choir this year.
One of my friend is joining the school choir this year.
questions.rule: One of + plural noun (friends), but the verb agrees with one: is.

options: What a exciting day it was!
What an exciting day it was!
How an exciting day it was!
questions.rule: What + a/an + adjective + noun; exciting starts with a vowel sound, so an.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After must never, use the base verb: must never copy.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The subject is Both the students (plural), so are going to.

questions.before: Rohan can swim now, but last year he
questions.rule: The past of can is could; last year needs the past.

questions.before: The teacher, along with her students,
questions.rule: With along with, the verb agrees with the first subject: The teacher is.
Question with going to: Are + you + going to + base verb ... ?
Exclamation: How + adverb + subject + verb !

chat: You look tired, Om. Is everything all right?
options: I can't slept well last night, ma'am.
I couldn't sleep well last night, ma'am.
I couldn't slept well last night, ma'am.
questions.rule: Past ability: couldn't + base verb (sleep), never slept after a modal.

chat: Your school bag looks heavy. Shall I carry some books for you?
options: Yes, please. My bag has too many books.
Yes, please. My bag have too many books.
Yes, please. My bag having too many books.
questions.rule: My bag is singular, so use has.
